correctness.rationale: The unitary Zak transform and Parseval on the unit torus give the exact multiplier Σ_j ∏_i |z_{β_i}(x_i−a_{j,i},ω_i)|², with no window normalization factor. The Jacobi product isolates a single zero (1/2,1/2), and differentiating its vanishing factor gives the stated negative spatial derivative and its nonzero imaginary frequency counterpart. The common-zero criterion is a coordinate cover: distinct residues let d coordinates kill at most d windows; a repeated residue kills two, leaving d−1 windows for the other coordinates. For the lower bound the open danger arc contains at most one residue per coordinate. For the remaining window the isolated factor has modulus at least 1−q_i^{ρ_i}; the first sequence of other factors is bounded by 1−q_i^{2n−1}, and the second sequence starting at n=2 by 1−q_i^{2n−3}, which gives the second copy of the odd product. The upper series bound follows by separating the two terms closest to x in a unit cell from both tails. For the planar family the common zero at ε=0 is unique modulo the periods. The nonvanishing factors there have modulus ℓ_β (by half-frequency evenness and unit-modulus quasi-periodicity). The local squared linear terms minimize at u=ε/2 and s=v=t=0, with value ℓ_β²D_β²ε²/2. Uniform convergence first localizes the global minimizers by compactness. In that neighborhood the quadratic term is bounded below by c||y||²−Cε² in local displacement y, so the Taylor error can be absorbed and the trial point forces ||y||=O(ε). Thus the Taylor error at any minimizer is o(ε²), proving the global sharp coefficient.
residual_risks: Finite Zak-series diagnostics do not prove the classification or global limit. The explicit bounds are conservative and the collision coefficient is for the specified planar family at fixed β only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Existence of some smooth Zak tuple (or a Parseval tuple) is not a classification of all d+1-tuples of pure Gaussian shifts. An obstruction for at most d windows does not select the solutions at d+1.

originality.rationale: Pass the classification of a prescribed minimal tuple of single time translates of a tensor Gaussian, together with its explicit bounds and planar boundary coefficient. Do not credit the minimum number of Schwartz windows in general, the Zak characterization, or uniqueness of the one-dimensional Gaussian Zak zero as new. The earlier existence theorems and related window families examined do not classify this exact prescribed family or give its sharp coefficient.
residual_risks: The bounded primary and catalogue searches do not exclude an older equivalent pure-translate theorem or a quantitative stability result. The standard Zak ingredients and general minimal-window threshold are not credited as new.

value.rationale: The criterion gives an exact feasibility check and explicit designs among all prescribed minimal pure-Gaussian tuples, not simply the prior existential threshold. The quantitative estimate supplies a practical positive bound from coordinate separations, and the planar law identifies the leading effect of a near-collision on the best lower frame bound. The exact coefficient captures more than detecting a common zero or observing decay on a grid.
residual_risks: The general lower estimate is not claimed optimal, and the sharp law does not cover arbitrary Gaussian or lattice perturbations.
